environment: Local loopback Phoenix server, disposable PostgreSQL database, synthetic simple-approval records, Chromium through Playwright Core 1.64.1 and Node 24.22.0

method.assets: mix assets.deploy; compressed and uncompressed assets rebuilt together
method.typing: Wait for the initial immediate draft acknowledgement and locked-input DOM restoration, then type 16 characters at 10 ms intervals and await the draft acknowledgement. Count outgoing LiveView draft events without retaining field values.
method.immediate_submit: Dispatch an input event and requestSubmit in the same JavaScript evaluation, before the 250 ms debounce can fire; reload and verify the persisted final value.

correctness: The first edit is immediate; the server establishes dirty-state guards before subsequent draft text is debounced.
Immediate Save persists the full submitted values even if the final draft event has not run.
A transition persists its current required reason without a preceding reason-change event.
A peer save preserves focus, local text and observed revisions until explicit conflict reapply.
Disconnect/reconnect restores the pending draft without automatically submitting a mutation.
Current authorization and visibility-removal paths remain covered by the full regression suite.
limitations: The first draft edit is not debounced. Measurements begin after its acknowledgement and DOM restoration.
Native blur, submit and DOM patch behavior can flush pending input earlier; this is not a hard per-second event limit.
This increment applies to staff-record draft fields and transition reasons; other FieldInput callers retain their existing behavior unless they opt in.
Browser event counts do not establish hosted latency, database CPU savings or concurrency capacity.
diagnostics: Early browser runs exposed blur-triggered flushes while initial locked inputs were still being restored and stale local compressed assets. The final controlled measurement uses current production assets and a settled initial acknowledgement; five repetitions produce the same result.
